brief: The S&P 500 rose 2.5% last week, its first weekly gain in five weeks and the largest since August, as investors weighed fundamentals against tech, inflation and geopolitics news. This week brings NVIDIA Q3 earnings, an AI developer Nasdaq IPO, multiple Fed speakers and a Xi-Trump-Putin APEC meeting; UBS expects volatility to stay elevated but fundamentals constructive enough to stay invested. UBS retains conviction in the structural AI opportunity (no single-name view), forecasting $1tr AI capex this year and $1.4tr in 2027 with accelerating cloud revenue growth, but flags chip-restriction uncertainty and financing/execution risk as reasons for selectivity and diversification. October core PPI rose 0.3% m/m (slowing from an upwardly revised 0.8% in September) even as CPI ran hot, raising the risk the Fed shifts to consecutive 25bp hikes; UBS expects this week's Fed speakers to sound more balanced than Logan's and Waller's recent hawkishness, and still likes high-quality fixed income at current yields. UBS says geopolitical breakthroughs are unlikely soon and portfolios shouldn't be adjusted solely for geopolitics; commodities, hedge funds and real assets can cushion shocks. Japan's Q3 GDP contracted 0.1% annualized, missing the 0.3% growth consensus on weaker consumption and an oil-import drag, but UBS calls this transitory and still expects BOJ hikes in December 2026 and March 2027.
